 Another Day, Another Ford Recall! This Time, It’s the Ford F-Series Trucks
 Olivia Richman 
 Oct 21, at 11:13am ET
 Share this article
 WhatsApp 
 Add us on Google 
 The Box AI Keys Questions 4 Vehicles 2 Ford's 81st recall of 2025 is for F-Series trucks, and while it sounds alarming, the actual issue — analog gauge needles going haywire — reveals something more interesting about how Ford operates than it does about truck safety. Over 102,000 vehicles are affected across the full F-Series lineup, from the F-150 all the way to the F-750 Super Duty, but one number buried in the data is genuinely hard to believe. Ford fired two-thirds of its leadership to fix its quality problem, and yet the recalls keep piling up — which raises a real question about whether this strategy is actually working or just shifting the burden onto owners. If you own an F-Series or are about to buy one, understanding why Ford keeps recalling vehicles at this pace matters more than the headlines suggest. Ask The Box → Considering the F-150 ? F-150 vs rival? Best trim Real MPG 01 Ford F-150 02 Ford Super Duty AI-generated summary from reviews, comparisons and articles by AutoNotion 
 Ford is known for its recalls. The automaker had over 580 recalls in 2025 .
 This doesn’t mean every recall is serious. And it doesn’t mean every recall is even bad. Ford – and other automakers – will often voluntarily recall vehicles when they feel there’s something that should be taken care of.
 However, Ford did fire two-thirds of its leadership in an attempt to improve quality control. Any boss who said a vehicle was “good enough” had to go. Instead of releasing vehicles that later fall on the customer to repair, Ford wanted to be more like Toyota , where it makes sure everything is as good as can be before it sells.
 While quality has improved, the recalls haven’t. Ford reached 80 recalls this year. Well, 81 if you count the most current one.
 The F-Series recall that sorta doesn’t matter
 The current recall is for Ford’s F-Series pickup trucks. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has issued Recall 26V653, which addresses an issue with analog gauges in F-Series trucks. Apparently, the needles are getting stuck or moving around wildly.
 The recall affects 102,159 vehicles. This includes trucks across the entire range, even the F-750 Super Duty. This includes the following vehicles produced between December 2024 and April 2026:
 F-250: 43,300
 F-350: 26,354
 F-450: 6,847
 F-600: 2,827
 Then, there is a pickup truck from 2026:
 F-150: 10,570
 There is one more:

 F-750 Super Duty: 1
 Yes, just one.
 This is yet another Ford recall that isn’t all too serious. There are a lot of those. And they can still be a pain in the butt since customers have to go to a dealership and get it fixed. Ford could have easily chosen not to announce a recall, but the automaker didn’t want to risk anyone getting distracted or annoyed while driving.
 Again, most recalls – including Ford’s – are not catastrophes. Despite its recalls, Ford is outperforming many other automakers in brand loyalty and safety. That’s because all of these seemingly insignificant recalls continue to make their vehicles safer.
 But does it have to be at the expense of the driver?
